topic: Adversarial pass on analyst post-event magnetic-bucket results draft (PRED-095/TIER-1/TIER-3/R005 verdict recommendations + SC-1..SC-4) before any verdict lands or the results file is OTS-stamped
current_verdict_holds_note: Refers to the DRAFT's recommended verdicts (PRED-095 falsified; PRED-TIER-1 falsified; PRED-TIER-3/R005 tacit_withdrawal; OBS-D-02 fires as-if). The live predictions.json entries are still pending and should stay pending until the revisions below are made. Do NOT commit predictions/eclipse-2026-08-12-results.json or request the operator OTS stamp on the current draft.
our_argument_summary: The draft (monitor/analyst/analysis-records/eclipse-2026-08-12-magnetic-results-DRAFT-20260926T072322.json:headline) argues that raw H-component deviations of -13 to -19 nT at the dome-cited stations are a pre-existing storm-recovery offset, that the eclipse-attributable signal after a post-hoc linear detrend is within about +/-5 nT of zero everywhere, and therefore recommends PRED-095 and PRED-TIER-1 be marked falsified (monitor/analyst/analysis-records/eclipse-2026-08-12-magnetic-results-DRAFT-20260926T072322.json:prediction_level.PRED_TIER_1), PRED-TIER-3/R005 tacit_withdrawal, and publishes four self-corrections (monitor/analyst/analysis-records/eclipse-2026-08-12-magnetic-results-DRAFT-20260926T072322.json:self_corrections). The arithmetic reproduces exactly (see curmudgeon_reproduction). The problems are in what is being tested and how the verdicts are labelled: the dome's Tier-1 claim is a Z-component, contact-phase-timed, Kp<2-gated prediction (monitor/baseline/03-predictions.txt:Instrument: Public INTERMAGNET 1-min Z-component) and the draft evaluates H-component timing against max coverage; the Kp<2 gate is honored for our own B1-M-001 but not for the dome; and our own pre-registered magnetic criteria turn out to fire (OBS-D-02) or fail to fire (OBS-S-02) on ordinary non-eclipse days, so the magnetic bucket is non-diagnostic for both models rather than a dome falsification.

dome_code_analysis.calculation_pipeline: Dome Tier-1 (registered 2026-04-08, V51.0): -17 to -21 nT umbra-locked dB at >=3 priority stations on the INTERMAGNET 1-min Z-component, pattern Y up / X down / Z down / F down, r > 0.7 with umbra contact geometry; falsification only on a verified Kp<2 day. Contact-phase prediction: signal peaks at C1 and C4, not at totality maximum. Dome live-scoring entry (as captured by analyst, not independently snapshotted this run): dB = -18.22 x coverage x FSF, predicted -28.9 nT at EBR/SPT, observed PENDING.
dome_code_analysis.hardcoded_vs_computed: Per the draft capture, observed remains the literal PENDING 46 days after the event; no fetch path evaluated. Not re-verified this run (live artifact; see hole on snapshot discipline).
data_sources_used: INTERMAGNET via BGS GIN (dome names it as the data source)
dome_code_analysis.escape_clauses: Two explicit dome escape clauses bear directly on this evaluation: (1) Tier-1 falsification only on a verified Kp<2 day; (2) Tier-3 success requires Kp < 2 for the entire Aug 9-12 window. GFZ definitive Kp: 2026-08-12 18-21 UT = 2.333; 2026-08-11 15-18 UT = 3.0. Both dome preconditions failed.
dome_code_analysis.code_discrepancies: The draft treats the dome prediction as an H-component, max-coverage-timed signal. The dome text specifies Z-component and C1/C4 contact-phase timing. Also: -18.22 = -10.9 x 1.672 (kappa) and -28.9 = -18.22 x 0.95 x 1.672, i.e. kappa is substituted for EBR FSF (dome table FSF 1.029 would give -17.8). The draft/ISS-3090 frame this as "two baselines"; it is kappa applied twice, corroborating WIN-010.c16 hole 6.

holes_found.description: The PRED-TIER-1 "falsified" verdict tests a claim the dome did not make. The dome's Tier-1 registration (monitor/baseline/03-predictions.txt:TIER 1 — Magnetic Signal (Globe-Compatible)) specifies (a) the INTERMAGNET 1-min Z-component, pattern Z down, and (b) timing against "umbra contact geometry", with the ECM-unique timing claim that the signal peaks at C1 and C4, NOT at totality maximum (same file, "Contact-phase prediction"). The draft evaluates the H-component only (monitor/analyst/analysis-records/eclipse-2026-08-12-magnetic-results-DRAFT-20260926T072322.json:methods.data), defines "umbra-locked" as tracking each station's max-coverage minute (monitor/analyst/analysis-records/eclipse-2026-08-12-magnetic-results-DRAFT-20260926T072322.json:prediction_level.PRED_TIER_1), and its eclipse-isolating detrend fits the trend line through [C1-60, C1] and [C4, C4+60] (monitor/analyst/analysis-records/eclipse-2026-08-12-magnetic-results-DRAFT-20260926T072322.json:methods.supplementary_metric_NOT_PREREGISTERED) - i.e. precisely the windows where the dome predicts its peaks - then scores only t_max +/- 30 min, where the dome predicts no peak. A dome defender can say, correctly, that we measured the wrong component at the wrong time and subtracted the predicted signal as "trend". Published as-is, this hands the author a legitimate strawman charge against our flagship pre-registered test.
holes_found.recommendation: Re-evaluate PRED-TIER-1 and PRED-095 on the Z-component (the dome's named instrument) and against a C1/C4 contact-phase template, with the detrend anchored away from C1/C4 (or no detrend; see hole 4). Keep the H-component analysis as the evaluation of OUR frozen protocol (which specified H). The curmudgeon quick reproduction (curmudgeon_reproduction.z_component) indicates the dome claim fails MORE cleanly on Z (raw protocol-style dZ peaks -4.1 to +8.8 nT, 5 of 7 stations positive, none within 10 nT of -17..-21), so this fix strengthens rather than weakens the conclusion - but it must be the analyst's reproduced number, not ours, that is published.

holes_found.description: Asymmetric use of the Kp<2 gate. For our own B1-M-001 the draft says "Kp precondition unmet so this is not a formal falsification" (monitor/analyst/analysis-records/eclipse-2026-08-12-magnetic-results-DRAFT-20260926T072322.json:self_corrections SC-1), while for the dome it recommends PRED-095 "falsified (conditions-qualified)" and PRED-TIER-1 "FAILS independent of Kp" (monitor/analyst/analysis-records/eclipse-2026-08-12-magnetic-results-DRAFT-20260926T072322.json:prediction_level). The dome's own falsification clause is explicitly Kp-gated ("No coherent signal at >=3 stations with r > 0.5 on verified Kp<2 day", monitor/baseline/03-predictions.txt:Falsification (Tier 1)) and its live countdown says "Requires Kp < 2" (raw-text/08-live-power.txt:190). GFZ definitive Kp for 18-21 UT on 2026-08-12 is 2.333 (verified this run). Our catalog has previously criticized the dome's Kp<2 clause as an escape hatch (data/predictions.json:PRED-TIER-3 detail_reasoning "the Kp<2 escape clause in monitor.py") and WIN-010.c16 hole 1 already flagged the symmetric-Kp problem. Excusing our range while falsifying theirs under the same failed precondition is the exact double standard a defender will quote.
holes_found.recommendation: Apply one rule to both sides. Either (A) both predictions are "untested - pre-registered Kp<2 precondition failed" with a detectability note for each, or (B) both are evaluated as-if with the same label strength (PRED-095 "not confirmed / disfavoured" AND B1-M-001 "not confirmed"). A defensible "falsified" for the dome should rest only on Kp-independent evidence: pre-first-contact timing (stronger_arguments #1) and the Z-component sign/magnitude (hole 1), each reported with the same caveats we give our own range.

holes_found.description: Our pre-registered magnetic criteria are miscalibrated in a way that favours us, and the draft reports OBS-D-02 as firing without disclosing it. Curmudgeon reproduction of the exact protocol metric (max |signed deviation| within +/-60 min of each station's t_max, quiet-day baseline, leave-one-out) on NON-eclipse days: the OBS-D-02 test (|peak - dome central| > 2 nT) fires at 7/7 dome stations on 2026-07-19, 2026-08-07 and 2026-08-11, 5/7 on 2026-08-06, 4 of 5 evaluable on 2026-07-31 - the >=5 quorum is met on 4 of 5 control days. Meanwhile OBS-S-02 (|peak| < 1 nT at every high-obscuration station, predictions/eclipse-2026-08-12-predictions.json:bucket_3_falsification_criteria.falsifies_standard_physics) is met at 0/7 stations on every day tested; with a 2 nT pre-committed noise floor (predictions/eclipse-2026-08-12-predictions.json:noise_floor_pre_commitment) it can never fire. On 2026-08-06 (Kp 0.333, one of our five quiet days) the protocol metric returns -5.9 to -18.3 nT at the dome stations, LER -18.3 nT, inside PRED-095's -17..-21 range. The dome-falsifier was near-certain to fire and the standard-physics falsifier could not fire. The draft notes OBS-D-03 has "essentially no power" but is silent on OBS-D-02/OBS-S-02.
holes_found.recommendation: Add SC-5 to the results file: "Our frozen magnetic criteria lacked a null calibration. OBS-D-02 (2 nT, >=5/9) fires on ordinary non-eclipse days; OBS-S-02 (|peak| < 1 nT) is below our own 2 nT noise floor and cannot fire. The OBS-D-02 result on 2026-08-12 carries no evidential weight." Change OBS-D-02 from "FIRES as-if" to "fired, non-diagnostic (fires on control days)". Upgrade OBS-O-02 from PARTIAL to FIRED: the magnetic bucket was not a clean test of either model and we say so plainly. Publish the control-day table alongside.

holes_found.description: The post-hoc detrended metric compares a +/-30-min window MEAN against PEAK-amplitude predictions and systematically attenuates any eclipse signal with E-region recovery lag. Injection test (obscuration-shaped signal, first-order recovery lag tau, same anchors and window as the draft): recovered fraction of the window mean is 100% at tau=0, ~96% at 15 min, ~84% at 30 min, ~62% at 60 min; and a signal with peak P has a window mean of only ~0.66P (tau=0) to ~0.41P (tau=60). Our own B1-M-001 cites a 60-180 min recovery timescale (predictions/eclipse-2026-08-12-predictions.json:bucket_1_standard_physics.magnetic_predictions). Consequences: (i) "No station within 10 nT of the range" (monitor/analyst/analysis-records/eclipse-2026-08-12-magnetic-results-DRAFT-20260926T072322.json:prediction_level.PRED_095.eclipse_isolated) overstates - a -17 nT-peak lagged signal would appear as roughly -7 nT, about 2-2.6 null-SD from the EBR/SPT residuals, not 10+ nT; (ii) SC-1 ("no station shows an eclipse-attributable dip of >=5 nT ... our range looks miscalibrated high") is partly an artifact - a -5 nT-peak signal at tau=60 appears as about -2 nT, matching EBR -2.2, SPT -3.2, GUI -2.4, SFS -5.0; (iii) the headline "within about +/-5 nT of zero at every pre-registered station" is not robust: a pre-contact-only linear extrapolation (no post-C4 anchor) gives ESK -6.9 and SFS -6.6.
holes_found.recommendation: Report the detrended metric as a peak-equivalent (or state predictions as window-means), publish an injection-recovery table so readers see the metric's sensitivity, add the pre-contact-only variant to the sensitivity set, and soften the headline to "no eclipse signal distinguishable from ordinary day-to-day variability". Rewrite SC-1 to: "our range was not scaled for a sunset eclipse and the data cannot confirm it; the observed Iberian residuals are compatible with the low end of our range under a lagged-recovery model and with zero".

holes_found.description: Registered predictions are omitted from the scorecard. (a) B2-M-002 - "8/9 dome stations should record |dB| < 2 nT" (predictions/eclipse-2026-08-12-predictions.json:registered_predictions_summary) - is never scored. It is the registered prediction the draft's own detrended result most resembles (|residual| < 2 nT at CLF, HAD, NGK, ESK; 2.2-3.2 nT at EBR, GUI, LER, SPT). A defender will note that we buried the one prediction that came closest. (b) B1-G-005 (Hartland 88% +/- 2 pp) is filed as a self-correction pending verification rather than scored as a failed registered claim; see hole 6.
holes_found.recommendation: Score every registered ID in the results file, B2-M-001, B2-M-002 and B1-G-005 included. For B2-M-002, state that the result is non-discriminating: near-zero residuals are also what a sunset-eclipse Chapman-Sq response predicts (SC-1), and B2-M-002 is our derivation of what dome geometry forces, which contradicts the dome's own -10.9/-18.22 formula anyway (the trilemma).

holes_found.description: SC-3 is now independently confirmed and must be upgraded from "verify first" to "our registered claim failed". The draft asks for a NASA-calculator cross-check before any prose edit (monitor/analyst/analysis-records/eclipse-2026-08-12-magnetic-results-DRAFT-20260926T072322.json:self_corrections SC-3). An independent ephemeris (timeanddate.com local circumstances for Bideford, ~12 km from Hartland, fetched this run) gives partial 17:17-19:08 UT, maximum 18:14 UT, magnitude 0.947, duration 1 h 51 min, agreeing with the draft's DE421 value (94.4% obscuration, 17:18-19:08). B1-G-005 (88% +/- 2 pp) fails its own registered tolerance by about 4 pp beyond the bound, and the published 'roughly 2 h 45 min' partial duration in data/sections.json part4 section 4.2.7 is about 55 min too long. PRED-ECLIPSE-2026-GEOMETRY currently reads as a clean standard-physics sweep of the geometric bucket (data/predictions.json:PRED-ECLIPSE-2026-GEOMETRY notes); one of our own B1 geometric claims actually failed. This overlaps WIN-010.c16 hole 4 (ISS-3082).
holes_found.recommendation: Record B1-G-005 as FAILED (outside registered tolerance) in the results file and a dated addendum, and correct section 4.2.7 (88% -> about 94%; 2 h 45 min -> about 1 h 50 min) plus docs/eclipse-2026 via the decider with a dated erratum note. Add one sentence to PRED-ECLIPSE-2026-GEOMETRY: the headline falsification (294 km vs 1.3 km) is unaffected, but our Hartland obscuration claim missed its own bound. If practical, add the NASA local-circumstances value as a third source; it is no longer a blocker.

holes_found.description: The ring-current attribution is asserted more strongly than the evidence supports. The headline says the depression "tracks a storm-recovery ring-current offset (Dst ~12-15 nT below the quiet-day baseline)" (monitor/analyst/analysis-records/eclipse-2026-08-12-magnetic-results-DRAFT-20260926T072322.json:headline). Station H responds to the ring current roughly as Dst x cos(magnetic latitude), which is about 0.55-0.75 at these stations, so a 12-15 nT Dst offset implies about 7-11 nT, not 12-15. The offset is also not uniform: LER's 14-16 UT mean is -4.1 nT against a window mean of -11.2 (monitor/analyst/analysis-records/eclipse-2026-08-12-magnetic-results-DRAFT-20260926T072322.json:per_station LER), so "the same depression was present two hours before" does not hold at LER. And the quietest control day (2026-08-06, Kp 0.333) shows protocol-metric values of -6 to -18 nT with no storm at all (hole 3), so ordinary day-to-day Sq variability can produce these magnitudes by itself.
holes_found.recommendation: Lead with what is empirical: the raw magnitudes are not distinctive (control days show the same) and most stations were already depressed before first contact. Present the storm-recovery ring current as a plausible contributor with the cos(lambda_m) scaling, and name LER as the exception.

holes_found.description: Tacit_withdrawal for PRED-TIER-3 and PRED-R005 does not carry over from the PRED-105 precedent. (1) The dome's own Tier-3 success criteria require "Kp < 2 entire Aug 9-12 window" (monitor/baseline/03-predictions.txt:Kp < 2 entire Aug 9–12 window); GFZ has Kp 3.0 on 2026-08-11 15-18 UT, so by the dome's own terms the test was void, not abandoned. (2) PRED-105's tacit_withdrawal leaned on an actively committing author (data/predictions.json:PRED-105 detail_reasoning, "silence is policy not infrastructure failure"). Here the analyst record shows no manual dome commit for 161 days (monitor/analyst/analysis-records/analysis-20260926-eclipse-magnetic-eval-plus-batch-105-changes.json:change_records_reviewed), so the silence is site-wide and says nothing specific about these two predictions. (3) We have not looked at the data ourselves, and our own evaluation was 15 days late (SC-4).
holes_found.recommendation: Keep PRED-TIER-3 and PRED-R005 pending with a dated note: "dome precondition (Kp<2 for Aug 9-12) failed; dome silent; data not yet evaluated by us". Revisit if IGETS Level-3 or ELF reductions become available. Do not set author_status to dome_silent_terminal on the strength of a site-wide drought.

holes_found.description: GUI is removed from OBS-O-01 by post-hoc judgment. OBS-O-01 fires if any observed signed peak is < -50 nT (predictions/eclipse-2026-08-12-predictions.json:bucket_3_falsification_criteria.falsifies_our_analysis). The GUI protocol value is -92.4 nT, which meets the letter of our own falsifier; the draft sets it aside as a publication-state artifact (monitor/analyst/analysis-records/eclipse-2026-08-12-magnetic-results-DRAFT-20260926T072322.json:criteria.OBS_O_01). The exclusion is correct (curmudgeon check: an August-only, same-publication-state baseline gives -19.6 nT, and GUI's August variation data still sits about -36 nT pre-eclipse, so the file is unstable). But setting aside the only datum that trips a falsifier of OUR analysis, with no pre-stated rule, is an optics problem we should close ourselves.
holes_found.recommendation: State a data-quality rule and apply it everywhere: stations whose baseline mixes publication states with a level step larger than X nT are excluded from the protocol metric for ALL criteria (OBS-D-02 counts, PRED-095 tallies, OBS-O-01). Say explicitly that GUI met the letter of OBS-O-01 and why it was excluded, with the same-state baseline result as evidence.

holes_found.description: Stronger argument missed on the dome live-scoring arithmetic (feeds ISS-3090/EXP-685). The draft calls -18.22 vs -10.9 nT "two eclipse formulas in one model" (monitor/analyst/analysis-records/eclipse-2026-08-12-magnetic-results-DRAFT-20260926T072322.json:prediction_level.dome_live_scoring_entry). The arithmetic is sharper than that: 10.9 x 1.672 = 18.22, and 18.22 x 0.95 x 1.672 = 28.9. The live entry's -28.9 nT at EBR uses kappa (1.672) in place of FSF, applied on top of a baseline that already includes kappa. The dome's own table lists EBR FSF as 1.029 (monitor/baseline/03-predictions.txt:EBREbro, Spain95%1.029), which would give -17.8 nT. This matches WIN-010.c16 hole 6 ("double-applied 1.672").
holes_found.recommendation: Replace the "two baselines" framing in the results file and in the ISS-3090/EXP-685 prose with the kappa-double-application finding, cross-referenced to WIN-010.c16.

holes_found.description: The draft cites a live dome artifact that has no repo snapshot: "captured_from https://john09289.github.io/predictions/data/status_history.json record 2026-09-26T06:41:29Z" (monitor/analyst/analysis-records/eclipse-2026-08-12-magnetic-results-DRAFT-20260926T072322.json:prediction_level.dome_live_scoring_entry). Under the citation-shape rules (monitor/prompts/reference/state-verification.md:Never cite a live dome-site artifact) this must be snapshotted before it is published.
holes_found.recommendation: Snapshot the eclipse entry (or the whole status_history.json) into data/dome-api-snapshots/ with its fetch timestamp, and cite the snapshot.

holes_found.description: Overgeneralized simultaneity wording. The companion analysis record says the dips run "from Portugal to Romania" (monitor/analyst/analysis-records/analysis-20260926-eclipse-magnetic-eval-plus-batch-105-changes.json:kernel_of_truth), but no Portuguese station was evaluated (COI has no data). Not every protocol peak falls at 17:09 or 18:47 either: LER 17:25, SFS 19:35, GUI 19:39 (monitor/analyst/analysis-records/eclipse-2026-08-12-magnetic-results-DRAFT-20260926T072322.json:per_station). The simultaneity point holds for the 17:09 group (NGK, WNG, BEL) and the 18:46-18:48 group (EBR, SPT, ESK, HAD, CLF, MAB, DOU, SUA).
holes_found.recommendation: Say "from Spain to Romania", name the two station groups, and list the exceptions.

holes_found.description: Quiet-day selection is under-documented. Station sets differ (EBR, CLF, BEL and SFS use 4 days without 2026-08-01; the others use 5) and the draft does not say why (monitor/analyst/analysis-records/eclipse-2026-08-12-magnetic-results-DRAFT-20260926T072322.json:per_station quiet_days_used). The protocol's "Kp <= 1" is read as max 3-h Kp <= 1.0; whether 1+ (1.333) qualifies is not stated (monitor/analyst/analysis-records/eclipse-2026-08-12-magnetic-results-DRAFT-20260926T072322.json:methods.quiet_days).
holes_found.recommendation: Add a sentence per station on why a day was dropped (data gap or publication state), and state the Kp <= 1 interpretation explicitly.

stronger_arguments.description: Pre-first-contact timing (Kp-independent, and valid under ANY timing reading of "umbra-locked"). The 17:09 UT protocol-metric peaks (the largest departure in each station's +/-60 min window) at NGK, WNG and BEL come before first contact at those same stations (computed C1: NGK 17:16-17:17, WNG 17:13-17:14, BEL 17:15-17:16; monitor/analyst/analysis-records/eclipse-2026-08-12-magnetic-results-DRAFT-20260926T072322.json:per_station partial_phase_ut). A magnetic excursion recorded before the Moon's penumbra reaches a station cannot be caused by the eclipse under either model. This is a cleaner discriminator than "LER peak precedes its max coverage", which a contact-phase reading of the dome claim would absorb.

Z-component on the dome's own named instrument. Protocol-style quiet-day-baseline dZ peaks within +/-60 min of t_max: EBR -4.1, SPT +1.4, HAD +5.1, CLF +2.2, NGK +5.6, ESK +4.6, LER +8.8 nT. None is near -17..-21, and 5 of 7 have the wrong sign for the dome's stated "Z down" pattern. This does not depend on the post-hoc detrend or on the ring-current attribution. (Curmudgeon quick computation - analyst must reproduce before citing.)

Control stations outside the eclipse. Hermanus (HER, zero obscuration) shows a ~2 nT drop over 18:40-18:53 UT, coinciding with the 18:41-18:46 drop across EBR, HAD, ESK, NGK, BEL and SUA, while night-side stations (KAK, HON, ABG) are flat. This supports a dayside/magnetospheric origin for the 18:4x feature, independent of eclipse geometry. Adding one or two non-eclipsed control stations turns the simultaneity argument from inference into demonstration.

The dome itself concedes Tier 1 cannot discriminate. It labels Tier 1 "Globe-Compatible" (monitor/baseline/03-predictions.txt:TIER 1 — Magnetic Signal (Globe-Compatible)) and says on WIN-068 that "Tier 1 is consistent with both models" (monitor/baseline/02-wins.txt:Tier 1 is consistent with both models). On the dome's own framing, even a Tier-1 hit would not have confirmed the dome over standard physics. That supports "standard_physics" as a defensible verdict for PRED-095, as an alternative to "falsified", and it is consistent with PRED-095's existing restates-WIN-068 note.

Suggested honest headline for the results file: "The magnetic sub-test was non-diagnostic for both models. Our pre-registered peak metric returns similar magnitudes on quiet non-eclipse days. Neither the dome's -17 to -21 nT nor our -5 to -25 nT is detectably present, the dome's named Z-component shows no eclipse-scale negative signal, and at several stations the largest departure in the window came before the eclipse reached them. The geometric sub-test (294 km vs 1.3 km) remains the decisive result - and one of our own geometric numbers (Hartland 88%) missed its bound."

kernel_of_truth.description: On the dome side: a total solar eclipse really does perturb ground magnetometers, and on 2026-08-12 the raw H-component at the dome's named Iberian stations did sit 13-16 nT below the quiet-day baseline during the eclipse window (monitor/analyst/analysis-records/eclipse-2026-08-12-magnetic-results-DRAFT-20260926T072322.json:per_station EBR protocol_peak_signed_dB_nT -13.69; SPT -15.6), reproduced exactly this run. The dome's insistence on a Kp<2 precondition is scientifically sensible: disturbed conditions do swamp eclipse signals, and this day was disturbed (GFZ Kp 2.333 for 18-21 UT). The dome also candidly labelled Tier 1 globe-compatible (monitor/baseline/03-predictions.txt:Globe-Compatible). On our side, the analyst draft is careful and mostly self-critical: it reports the protocol metric first, discloses the post-hoc detrend, the GUI artifact, the Kp failure and our own lateness (monitor/analyst/analysis-records/eclipse-2026-08-12-magnetic-results-DRAFT-20260926T072322.json:honest_limits).
kernel_of_truth.why_it_doesnt_save_claim: The raw depression is not an eclipse signature. The same protocol metric returns -6 to -18 nT at these stations on the quietest non-eclipse day (2026-08-06; curmudgeon_reproduction.control_days), several stations' sharpest dips came before first contact (NGK, WNG, BEL at 17:09; monitor/analyst/analysis-records/eclipse-2026-08-12-magnetic-results-DRAFT-20260926T072322.json:per_station), and the dome's own component (Z) shows mostly positive, small excursions (curmudgeon_reproduction.z_component). A precondition that failed also means the dome cannot claim a hit - its own rule only permits a verdict on a verified Kp<2 day (monitor/baseline/03-predictions.txt:Falsification (Tier 1)). The right conclusion is "no eclipse magnetic signal detected, test non-diagnostic under the conditions", applied equally to both models.

per_prediction_verdicts.reasoning: The Kp gate and the component mismatch (holes 1-2) plus the non-diagnostic protocol metric (hole 3) do not support "falsified" under a symmetric rule. Options, in order of preference: (a) standard_physics - the dome labels Tier 1 globe-compatible, and PRED-095 restates WIN-068 (Std Model Explains); add a note that the specific amplitude was not observed on Z or H; (b) keep pending with a dated "precondition failed; no signal detected" note. Use "falsified" only if B1-M-001 receives an equally strong label.

As argued, this tests H-component max-coverage timing, not the dome's Z-component C1/C4 contact template. After re-analysis on Z with a contact-phase template, the pre-C1 timing at NGK/WNG/BEL and the Z sign pattern may support "falsified" on Kp-independent grounds. The dome's own clause still gates falsification on Kp<2, so the note must say we are overriding the author's precondition and why (the claimed amplitude is far above the empirical noise).
The dome precondition (Kp<2 for all of Aug 9-12) failed, silence is site-wide (161-day manual drought), and we have not evaluated the data. Keep pending with a dated note (hole 8).
Same as PRED-TIER-3; no Kp-precondition text found for R005, but we have not evaluated the ELF data, so the verdict would rest only on author silence during a site-wide drought.

per_self_correction_verdicts.reasoning: The sunset-scaling point is right, but "no dip >= 5 nT" comes from comparing a window mean against a peak range with an attenuating detrend (hole 4). Reword so it neither confirms nor condemns our range.

deeper_analysis: Other side of the argument, stated fairly: the analyst could reply that (1) the frozen protocol specified H, so evaluating H is correct; (2) a -17..-21 nT signal is large enough to see even at Kp 2+, so the Kp gate is a formality; (3) the detrend is disclosed as post-hoc and reported second. Point (1) is right for OUR criteria (OBS-D-*, B1-M-001) and wrong for the DOME's predictions (PRED-095/TIER-1), which have their own registered component and timing. Point (2) is a legitimate detectability argument, but it cuts both ways: by the same logic the -5..-25 nT B1-M-001 range is testable at Kp 2+ and our own range must be labelled with the same strength, and the argument has to be quantified with an injection test, not asserted. Point (3) is fair, and it is why the draft is salvageable. On the dome side, the strongest defence is "precondition failed, test void". That is true by the dome's own words, and we should say so rather than let the author say it first. It does not rescue the dome: a void test is not a confirmation, and the dome's live scoring still reads PENDING 46 days out. The review's credibility rests on this file being visibly symmetric. The results file will be OTS-stamped and is the first post-event document the dome author is likely to read (per the author-contact context in CLAUDE.md). It should be the most careful document in the repo, not the fastest.
